problem.heading: The Year-End Reconciliation Crunch Is Unsustainable
paragraphs: Every January, property controllers face the same cycle: export GL data from Yardi or MRI, map hundreds of expense codes to CAM pools, calculate gross-ups for partially occupied buildings, apply administrative fees and caps, then allocate shares to dozens of tenants across multiple properties. A single building can take hours of spreadsheet work, and most portfolios have 20+ buildings that all need reconciliation before March deadlines.

The manual process is not just slow. It is error-prone. Misclassified GL codes, forgotten cap adjustments, and incorrect square footage inputs compound into billing errors. They erode tenant trust and leave recoverable dollars on the table. When tenants audit your statements and find mistakes, the cost in staff time, legal exposure, and relationship damage far exceeds the original error amount.

solution.heading: How CapVeri Automates Year-End Reconciliation
paragraphs: CapVeri ingests your GL export files directly. No API integration or ERP configuration required. Our parser recognizes Yardi, MRI, and generic CSV formats automatically. It maps expense codes to standardized CAM pools using BOMA 2024 methodology. Within minutes of uploading, you have a clear view of every expense category, with automatic classification suggestions and flagged anomalies.

From there, CapVeri runs deterministic financial calculations: gross-up adjustments for vacancy, administrative fee application, cap enforcement per lease terms, and pro-rata tenant share allocation. Every calculation traces back to the source GL line. What used to take your team weeks of spreadsheet work now happens in an afternoon.

problem.heading: Portfolio Scale Makes Manual Reconciliation Impossible
paragraphs: When you manage a single building, CAM reconciliation is tedious but manageable. At 10+ properties, the process breaks down. Each building has different expense structures, different lease terms, different cap provisions, and often different property management systems. Controllers end up maintaining dozens of independent spreadsheets with inconsistent methods, making it hard to ensure accuracy or meet deadlines across the portfolio.

The real cost is not just time. It is the lack of visibility. Portfolio managers cannot easily compare CAM expenses across buildings, identify properties with abnormal cost trends, or verify that reconciliation methods are consistent. When a tenant at Building A gets different treatment than an identical lease at Building B, it creates legal exposure and undermines credibility with institutional tenants.

solution.heading: How CapVeri Standardizes Portfolio-Wide Reconciliation
paragraphs: CapVeri gives you a single dashboard for every property in your portfolio. Upload GL exports from any combination of Yardi, MRI, or other systems, and each building gets the same BOMA 2024 aligned methodology. A mapping decision you make for one building automatically applies to similar codes in other buildings.

Portfolio-level reporting lets you compare CAM costs per square foot across buildings, spot outliers, and track year-over-year trends. When reconciliation season arrives, you can see exactly which buildings are complete, which need review, and which have flagged anomalies. All from one screen instead of chasing down spreadsheets from regional teams.

problem.heading: CAM Assumptions in Underwriting Are Often Wrong
paragraphs: Acquisition teams build pro formas based on the seller's reported CAM recovery ratios, but those numbers are frequently unreliable. Sellers may have miscategorized expenses, missed gross-up adjustments, or failed to enforce caps correctly. That inflates or deflates the apparent recovery rate. Without digging into the actual GL data and lease terms, buyers inherit billing errors that directly impact NOI and asset valuation.

Traditional due diligence relies on sampling: review a handful of tenant reconciliation statements and spot-check a few expense categories. This approach misses systemic issues like incorrect BOMA methodology, inconsistent allocation bases, or expense codes that have drifted between recoverable and non-recoverable pools over time. The result is acquisition models built on assumptions that do not hold up once you take ownership.

solution.heading: How CapVeri Powers Acquisition CAM Diligence
paragraphs: CapVeri lets you run an independent reconciliation on the acquisition target's GL data without needing access to their property management system. Request the seller's GL export for the past 2-3 years, upload it to CapVeri, and within hours you have a clear picture: what was spent, how it was classified, what should have been recovered, and where the gaps are.

The analysis goes beyond simple expense review. CapVeri compares the seller's implied recovery ratio against what the lease terms actually allow, identifies cap provisions that may compress future recoveries, and flags expense trends that suggest deferred maintenance or cost-shifting. Your acquisition team gets hard numbers for pricing negotiations and post-close budgeting.

solutions.headline: Find & Fix CAM Errors in Yardi Exports
solutions.subheadline: Yardi is powerful, but CAM configuration drift creates billing errors that compound silently. CapVeri catches what Yardi's built-in reports miss.

problem.heading: Yardi Configuration Drift Creates Silent Billing Errors
paragraphs: Yardi Voyager's CAM module is highly configurable, which is both its strength and its biggest risk. Over time, GL account mappings drift: new expense codes get added without proper pool assignments, chart of accounts restructuring breaks recovery group linkages, and staff turnover means the person who set up the original CAM configuration is long gone. The result is a system that runs calculations on incorrect inputs without any warning.

These errors are not obvious from Yardi's standard reports. A misclassified GL code might shift $50,000 from a recoverable pool to a non-recoverable one, silently reducing your CAM billings. Incorrect occupancy percentages in gross-up calculations, forgotten base year resets after lease renewals, and stale square footage figures all compound into material billing discrepancies. They only surface when a tenant hires an auditor. By that point you owe refunds plus interest.

solution.heading: How CapVeri Catches Yardi CAM Errors
paragraphs: CapVeri works as an independent check on top of your Yardi data. Export your GL report from Yardi (the same export you already run for reconciliation) and upload it to CapVeri. Our parser understands Yardi's export format natively, including account segments, property codes, and GL descriptions. CapVeri then independently classifies every expense line and runs its own reconciliation calculation.

By comparing CapVeri's independent results against what Yardi produced, you immediately see discrepancies. Misclassified GL codes, incorrect pool assignments, gross-up errors, and cap calculation mistakes all show up as line-item variances. CapVeri does not replace Yardi. It gives you confidence that Yardi's output is correct, and when it is not, it tells you exactly where to look and what to fix.

solutions.subheadline: Recovery ratios depend on your lease mix. Mixed portfolios often recover just 70-85%. CapVeri finds the gaps costing you money.

problem.heading: Revenue Leakage Hides in CAM Reconciliation Details
paragraphs: CAM recovery leakage rarely comes from one big mistake. It builds from dozens of small issues: an expense code mapped to the wrong pool, a gross-up calculation using the wrong occupancy percentage, a tenant whose cap was not updated after a lease amendment, or administrative fees never applied because the lease clause was missed during setup. Each issue might cost $2,000-$10,000 per year per building, but across a portfolio they add up to hundreds of thousands in lost revenue.

The challenge is visibility. Standard ERP reports show you what you billed, not what you should have billed. Without an independent check of every expense classification, every calculation input, and every lease provision, there is no way to know whether your recovery ratio is leaving money on the table. Most controllers suspect gaps but lack the time to find them.

solution.heading: How CapVeri Identifies and Closes Recovery Gaps
paragraphs: CapVeri calculates your theoretical maximum recovery: what you would bill if every eligible expense were correctly classified, every gross-up used accurate occupancy data, every cap were properly applied, and every administrative fee were charged per lease terms. It then compares this theoretical maximum against your actual billings to quantify the gap.

Each recovery gap is broken down by cause: misclassified expenses, incorrect gross-up inputs, missed administrative fees, or cap provisions that could be restructured at lease renewal. CapVeri sorts gaps by dollar impact so your team can focus on corrections that matter most. Over time, the platform tracks your recovery ratio trend and alerts you when new leakage appears.

faqs.question: What is a typical CAM recovery ratio?
faqs.answer: It depends on your lease structure. Full NNN leases recover 90% to 100%. Office properties with base-year structures recover 60% to 80%. Mixed portfolios often land between 70% and 85%. The gap between your ratio and your lease maximum is real money. CapVeri helps you recover it.

faqs.question: How quickly will I see results?
faqs.answer: The initial analysis takes 1-2 days per property. Most clients see their first recovery improvements within the current reconciliation cycle. Full optimization across a portfolio typically takes 4-6 weeks.

faqs.question: Does improving recovery require changing tenant lease terms?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Most recovery gaps come from internal errors: misclassified expenses, incorrect calculation inputs, or overlooked lease provisions that already entitle you to higher billings. You are recovering what your leases already allow.

faqs.question: Can I quantify recovery improvement for my CFO?
faqs.answer: Yes. CapVeri produces a recovery improvement report showing before and after recovery ratios, total dollar impact by building and portfolio, and the specific corrections that drove the improvement. This is designed for C-suite and investor reporting.

faqs.question: Will tenants push back on higher CAM billings?
faqs.answer: CapVeri ensures every billing is supported by accurate calculations and proper documentation. When billings increase because errors are corrected, the audit trail demonstrates that the new amounts are what the lease always entitled you to recover. This actually reduces dispute risk compared to sending out statements with known or suspected errors.
